The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:

Co. Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not able to do any work as earlier.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA- 57/F-2559.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Hoskote Traffic Police in Crime No.179/2023.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notice, the respondent has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to sole 4 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus.
It is contended that there is delay of 8 days in lodging the complaint.
Further denied the age, income, occupation of the petitioner and also expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.
It is also contention of the respondent that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 29.6.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. near Hosakote Toll, Bengaluru-Kolar road,
Hosakote, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2559 in an actionable negligence?

18. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.

The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1
to P13

Ex.P12-wound certificate, Ex.P13-true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.179/2023 of Hosakote Police.
19. It is pertinent to note that, there is 8 days delay in giving first information.
But on going 8 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 through the circumstance of the case and also injuries sustained by the petitioner, one cannot expect to give first information soon after the accident.
In this regard, in column No. 3(c) of the Ex.P1, there is a clear mention about the reason for delay in giving first information.
As per law, delay in giving first information is not always fatal.

20. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given one Shashikumar, the S.H.O. of Hosakote Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC R/W Section 187 of IMV Act.
21.
In order to substantiate the defence of the respondent, has examined its driver as RW1.
RW1 has reiterated the defence made in the written statement.

At the time of cross-examination of PW1, though several questions put to the witness, but nothing has been culled out from his mouth to believe all the defenses of the respondent forthcoming in the written statement.
Even at the time of cross-examination of RW1, though he has stated that false case has been registered against him.
But not placed any documents on record to prove the same.
The respondent herein, except making allegations against the petitioner, no supportive and reliable documents placed for consideration to believe his defenses against the case of the petitioner.
23. In the light of the discussions held above, I hold that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2559.
Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory materials on record, to prove the aforesaid issue.

Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative ISSUE NO.2 :

sentences.text: This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner 10 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

25. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

sentences.text: The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim 11 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced MLC marked as Ex.P12.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
Left heal pad avulsion with calcaneal exposure and contamination 27.
In connection with the above said injury, the doctor is of the opinion that the said injury is grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries and lab reports as per Ex.P14 & Ex.P26.

On going through the discharge summaries issued by Silicon Hospital, Bengaluru and Daya General Hospital,Thrissur marked at Ex.P14 reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 29.6.22023 to 7.7.2023, from 8.8.2023 to 9.8.2023 and from 11.9.2023 to 12.9.2023.
In addition to his evidence, placed the 12 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner had sustained Left foot complete tendon Avlsion with calcneum fracture with sepsis, for which he has placed OPD record and x-ray as per Ex.P27 & Ex.P28.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

It means he can continue his service in future also.
36. In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.

At the same time, it is to be noted that, due to the nature of the injuries 17 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 sustained by the petitioner, there would be some difficulty to him to do normal work, as he was earlier.

Hence, I relied the decision reported in, ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others, it was observed, that.
"The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.

sentences.text: The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labor market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre-accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers, this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first."

sentences.text: On perusal of the above said decision, it is observed that, though the claimant is in a position to 18 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.

38. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued his job, he has to suffer with the said disability throughout his life and the eligibility of his employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to his disability.

Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of reduced 19 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.

39.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to walk, sit, squat,
climb stairs cannot sit cross leg.

On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a Hotel business.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities.
40. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has not stated about future medication.

LIABILITY:
43.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2559, 21 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent being the owner as well as internal insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, the respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
44.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,79,063/- (Rupees four lakh seventy nine thousand and sixty three only), along with interest @ 6% per 22 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 29.6.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. near Hosakote Toll, Bengaluru-Kolar road,
Hosakote, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2559 in an actionable negligence?
Rakesh Elayath vs K S R T C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105888638/
2 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?
from whom?
3.
What order or award?
15 . It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA- 57/F-2559, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
16. On the other hand, it is the strong contention of the respondent that, on the date of accident the driver of the bus passing slowly towards left service road, the traffic police was present, the rider of the motor cycle came from said service road, the authorities showed their hand to stop the vehicle,
suddenly the rider of the motor bike he bcame tensed and due to fear he rode his vehicle and dashed against the bus, fell down and his leg caught 7 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 front left side tire, due to which he suffered injuries to his left leg.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As per law, delay in giving first information is not always fatal.
20. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given one Shashikumar, the S.H.O. of Hosakote Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of I.P.C.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC R/W Section 187 of IMV Act.
21.
In order to substantiate the defence of the respondent, has examined its driver as RW1.
But not placed any documents on record to prove the same.
The respondent herein, except making allegations against the petitioner, no supportive and reliable documents placed for consideration to believe his defenses against the case of the petitioner.
The petitioner 10 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim 11 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
Reduced disability of employment;
31.
It means he can continue his service in future also.
At the same time, it is to be noted that, due to the nature of the injuries 17 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 sustained by the petitioner, there would be some difficulty to him to do normal work, as he was earlier.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.
38. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued his job, he has to suffer with the said disability throughout his life and the eligibility of his employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to his disability.
As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent being the owner as well as internal insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of reduced 19 SCCH-18 MVC No.5012/2023 eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities.
41. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 40,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs.1,53,574-00 20 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 30,489-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 15,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,79,063/- (Rupees four lakh seventy nine thousand and sixty three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
Therefore, the respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,79,063/- (Rupees four lakh seventy nine thousand and sixty three only), along with interest @ 6% per 22 SCCH-18 MVC No. 5012/2023 annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
